eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs project a daytime high near 60–64°F for San Francisco on May 24, supported by a strengthening marine layer and persistent onshore westerly flow that limits afternoon warming. This coastal cooling effect, driven by cold Pacific upwelling and typical May fog patterns, keeps temperatures below the month’s long-term average high of 65–67°F. Trader consensus favoring 64°F or higher at 64.5% reflects the upper range of current forecasts, while the 28% probability on 62–63°F captures model spread and potential for thicker stratus. Historical analogs show similar late-May setups rarely exceed 70°F without offshore flow, and the next model update cycle will clarify whether any ridge strengthening can push readings across the key threshold.

The narrow market split between the 32°C and 33°C outcomes reflects minor uncertainties in boundary-layer mixing, exact timing of peak heating, and any residual thin cloud that could trim the high by 1°C. With resolution imminent, the next Météo-France and ECMWF model runs will likely tighten the range further as surface observations and upper-air data are assimilated.
